name: infective endocarditis overview
title: Infective endocarditis decision chart: blood cultures and echocardiography are counted against the modified Duke criteria, then the valve and the culture result (native valve, prosthetic valve or device, culture-negative) decide the likely organism, the echo route and the antibiotics; panels give the indications and timing for surgery and who gets dental prophylaxis

root.title: Fever + a damaged valve, a device, IV drug use or a new murmur: is it infective endocarditis (IE)?
lines: search every system for EMBOLI and for HEART FAILURE

groups.title: 1 · Three sets of blood cultures  →  2 · Transthoracic echo (TTE)  →  3 · Count the modified DUKE criteria
lines: cultures from 3 sites, all within the first hour if very sick; echo as soon as IE is suspected

pres.title: DEFINITE: 2 major, 1 major + 3 minor, or 5 minor  |  POSSIBLE: 1 major + 1 minor, or 3 minor  →  treat both
lines: • MAJOR: typical organism in 2 cultures, cultures persistently positive (> 12 h apart), Coxiella, or echo showing vegetation, abscess or new regurgitation
• MINOR: predisposing heart lesion or IV drug use, fever ≥ 38 °C, emboli (Janeway lesions), immune signs (Osler nodes, Roth spots)

head: h
Native valve IE
rheumatic, prolapsed, bicuspid or congenitally abnormal valve
h
Prosthetic valve or device IE
new fever after valve surgery = IE until proven otherwise
clue: • or a device with persistent fever
• even with no new murmur or bacteremia
inv: • cultures + echo BEFORE assuming another cause

head: h
Culture-negative IE
organisms that do not grow in routine bottles
inv: TTE, then TEE as for native valve

rows: 1 · Major ischemic stroke or intracranial hemorrhage?
YES → DELAY surgery at least 4 weeks
• heart failure from valve dysfunction or a fistula
• persistent infection, resistant organism (S. aureus, fungi), relapsing prosthetic IE
